note: Independent labels; split dev/test by id parity; never tune on test. Odd ids (wb001, wb003, ...) are dev, even ids are test. Requests are written the way people talk, not in catalogue words. anchor: 1-3 slugs that do the core of the ask (best first). steps: ordered groups; any slug in a group satisfies that position. before/after: acceptable slugs that would come right before/after the anchor. user_supplies: input types the person already has (port types from blocks.json portTypes). coverage: full | partial (catalogue can only do part of it well) | none (catalogue cannot do it; anchor and steps are empty and tools should decline rather than force a fit). ready_workflow: the closest ready workflow, or null. Self-check treats these input types as interchangeable: see type_compat.

goals.request: landing page for my facebook ad
goals.why: Site becomes a brand file, which plus the offer and the ad feeds the matched page; design direction and the 30-point review need the finished page.

goals.request: Can you write a few Facebook ads for my handmade soap? Mostly women over 30 who like that it's gentle on skin.
goals.why: Ad writers need a brief, so the buyer notes become a brief first; the drafted ads then go through a pre-launch or policy check.

goals.request: our facebook ads were fine then the last 2 weeks cost per sale basically doubled, we didn't change anything?? what happened
goals.why: Diagnosis needs only the exported results; its audit report is what the keep-or-change checker turns into a decision.

goals.request: get more customers
goals.why: Vague growth ask: profile the business, rank channels from the profile, plan one small channel test, then review results against the profile. Any one channel planner is fine in step 3.

goals.request: google ads for my plumbing business
goals.why: Most Google Ads items here are built for online stores; the generic search-ads planner fits a local service, then call and form tracking is checked on the site before spending. Mediocre fit for local-service specifics.

goals.request: I want to run two versions of my ad against each other and actually know which one won.
goals.why: The test plan comes from the two drafts; the reply offer is built from that plan; the result reader needs the live numbers the test produces.

goals.request: meta keeps rejecting my ad for a hair growth serum, says something about personal attributes?? how do i reword it so it runs
goals.why: The policy checker finds the flagged wording and rewrites it; a final pre-launch check reviews the rewritten ad before resubmitting.

goals.request: ugc style tiktok script for my skincare product
goals.why: Script writers take a brief; the script plus product facts make the filming brief a creator can shoot from.

goals.request: Give me like 20 different angles I could test in ads for my sleep gummies.
goals.why: Angle writers need a brief; the angle library they return is what the headline batch writer turns into testable hooks.

goals.request: launching an online course, have maybe $500 for ads total, no clue how to split it or what to test first
goals.why: Budget split and staging come from the question and product; the test campaign planner needs the brief from step 1. The small-budget planner is store-flavoured, so the calculator is the safer anchor for a course. The small test and rollout planner is the non-store option: it sizes a test you can afford to lose from the course price.

goals.request: ad fatigue fix
goals.why: The fading ad's numbers give the cause and fresh hook briefs; adding the new ads into the running campaign is planned from the same results.

goals.request: I need a simple report for my client showing how their ads did this month compared to last month.
goals.why: Two periods of numbers give the what-changed analysis first; the report writer turns the same sheet into the client document.

goals.request: people add stuff to cart then vanish. want ads that follow them and bring them back, we sell dog beds
goals.why: Reviews give the objections the retargeting ads answer; the objection map feeds the sequence; the budget cap is set last from store results.

goals.request: just run my facebook ads for me and change the budgets every day automatically
goals.why: Nothing in the catalogue logs into an ad account or changes budgets; the best fit is a daily keep/pause review the person applies by hand, then a budget split from the same results.

goals.request: here's my ad copy, is it any good before I put money behind it?
goals.why: The check produces an audit report; the fix writer needs that report plus the original ad to rewrite it.

goals.request: welcome email series for new subscribers
goals.why: The sequence writer turns the brief into five drafts; review, plain-English edit and the send-readiness score all work on those drafts in that order.

goals.request: tons of people get all the way to checkout on my shopify store and then just leave. want emails that pull them back without being annoying
goals.why: The flow is built from product facts; the gap checker reviews that flow's triggers and timing; the results reader needs send data once it runs.

goals.request: I want to send a monthly newsletter for my yoga studio but I never know what to write about.
goals.why: The real gap is topics, so a topic plan comes first; each issue is drafted from the brief, then subject lines and a send check work on the draft. The weekly newsletter agent covers the same chain.

goals.request: better subject lines so people actually open my emails
goals.why: Subject options come from the brief and the email body; the readiness check scores the email with its chosen subject.

goals.request: got about 4000 emails on my list but haven't sent anything in over a year. scared if i blast them now i'll land in spam. how do i restart
goals.why: Split the old list first so the safest group is mailed first; the re-engagement and suppression flow runs on that segment. A domain check (inbox delivery fixer) is a sensible add-on.

goals.request: I'm releasing an ebook next month. Write the emails that announce it and get people to actually buy.
goals.why: The launch sequence is built from the ebook facts and the launch offer; the review checks the drafted emails.

goals.request: when someone buys from my shop I want them added to my email list and sent a thank-you automatically. can you set that up?
goals.why: The catalogue can write the after-order emails and map the automation, but nothing here connects the person's shop and email tool for them.

goals.request: Can you check this email before I send it to my whole list?
goals.why: Review the draft first; the fix pass works on the same draft guided by what the review found.

goals.request: instagram posts for my bakery for the next month
goals.why: The platform content planner needs a brand file (made from the site, or from scratch with the messaging builder); it then returns the month of posts and openings.

goals.request: I post on LinkedIn every week and get like 3 likes each time. what am i doing wrong
goals.why: Diagnose the old posts first; a strategy with pillars comes next; new posts are written once the angle is set.

goals.request: Turn my hour-long YouTube video into a handful of shorts and some posts.
goals.why: Both the clip finder and the post writers need the transcript, so it is pulled first; clips are chosen, then the same transcript is repurposed into posts. The long-video workflow takes a transcript and ends in the clip finder, so it covers the shorts half.

goals.request: tiktok hooks for my product
goals.why: Hooks come from product facts; the ranker picks which ones to test first.

goals.request: I'd like to send free product to some smaller creators so they post about it.
goals.why: The gifting planner needs a brand file and benefits from a creator list, so both come first. The creator-gifting workflow also needs returned footage, so it is a later fit.

goals.request: grow my following
goals.why: Strategy turns the vague goal into a brief; posts are planned from that brief; results are read once posts have run.

goals.request: schedule and auto-post my stuff to instagram, facebook and tiktok every morning
goals.why: No item posts or schedules for the person; the catalogue can write platform versions and design a Zapier/Make/n8n automation they then set up themselves.

goals.request: my youtube channel has been stuck around 200 subscribers for months. is it my titles and thumbnails or something else?
goals.why: Title and thumbnail pairs are generated then ranked; the transcript is pulled so the retention reader can tie the viewer drop to what was said. The channel auditor answers the "titles or something else?" question directly (titles as a set, thumbnails, first 15 seconds) and can run once the transcripts are in.

goals.request: seo audit for my website
goals.why: The site review ranks problems first; technical and on-page passes follow; titles, descriptions and structured data are written last for the pages that need them.

goals.request: Why did my Google traffic drop by half last month?
goals.why: The drop is diagnosed from the search data export; once fixes are made the change tracker watches whether traffic recovers.

goals.request: I run a small dental clinic and want to show up when people nearby search for a dentist, like on google maps
goals.why: The local listing audit is the core; site pages are tuned for the area next; asking happy patients for reviews feeds the listing. Only one local-search item exists, so depth is limited.

goals.request: blog post ideas that will actually rank
goals.why: Keywords come first; each chosen keyword becomes a post brief; the post is written from that brief. The topic-cluster workflow covers steps 1-2.

goals.request: How do I get ChatGPT and the other AI assistants to recommend my business when people ask for the best one?
goals.why: Audit how AI answers see the site first; the gap finder ranks fixes from that audit; then publish machine-readable guidance. The store workflow needs product data, so the generic audit fits a non-store business better. The agentic search optimizer checks whether AI agents can complete tasks on the site, not whether assistants recommend it, so it is not a fit.

goals.request: we have like 300 old blog posts and traffic keeps sliding. should we delete some of them??
goals.why: Decay is found first, each page gets keep/refresh/cut from the traffic sheet, kept pages are refreshed and retitled, then the change tracker watches results.

goals.request: meta titles and descriptions for 40 product pages
goals.why: A single-step job: the writer takes product facts and returns titles and descriptions. Schema markup is a reasonable follow-on once the pages are live.

goals.request: get me backlinks from big sites, happy to pay for them
goals.why: Nothing buys links; the catalogue only plans earned links and PR outreach, which is the honest alternative.

goals.request: Help me write a cold email to local gyms offering my bookkeeping services.
goals.why: The cold email writer needs a buyer profile, so the gym-owner profile is written first; the draft then gets a pre-send check.

goals.request: sales call script
goals.why: The lead argument (angle library) feeds the short opener; objection answers come next; the closing questions use the offer.

goals.request: had a great call with a prospect 3 weeks ago, sent the proposal, now total silence. do i chase? how without being pushy
goals.why: The stall check produces a next-step plan; the yes-ladder turns that plan into low-pressure questions; calm reply lines are drafted from the plan.

goals.request: I just finished a discovery call, here's the transcript. Can you turn it into a proposal?
goals.why: Call notes become the follow-up and proposal inputs; the proposal document is then margin-checked and turned into a dated plan to signature.

goals.request: list of leads to reach out to
goals.why: The list is built from the buyer profile, ranked, then first messages are drafted and checked, and a daily outreach block is planned. List building may need paid data access.

goals.request: client says my price is too high and wants 30% off. I honestly can't afford to drop that much, what do I say to them
goals.why: Understand the client's side, set limits and a counter, prep the call, then draft calm replies. Either negotiation workflow fits; the weaker-side one matches a solo seller best.

goals.request: customers keep saying 'let me think about it' at the end of my calls. how do I handle that better?
goals.why: The stall line is an unspoken doubt, so build the objection sheet first; the closing questions are then planned around the offer.

goals.request: find me the personal cell numbers of CEOs at 500 companies in my niche
goals.why: No item gathers personal phone numbers, and it should not; prospect list builders work from company-level data. Tools should decline rather than force a list builder.

goals.request: product descriptions for my etsy candles
goals.why: Descriptions are written from product facts; a concrete-copy pass then sharpens vague lines using the same facts.

goals.request: we sell candles on shopify and returns are eating our margin, help
goals.why: Find which products are returned and why from the store data, cost the returns, then set a policy with the return costs in hand. The returns reviewer agent bundles steps 1-2.

goals.request: I want to open my first Shopify store this month. What do I actually need to do?
goals.why: Setup plan first; products and variants feed the collections and menu; shipping and tax are set before the go-live check and test order.

goals.request: find a winning product to sell online
goals.why: The scout returns candidates plus a competitor set, which the white-space finder needs; the chosen product is scored on costs, then a small test is planned.

goals.request: My product page gets visitors but hardly anyone buys. Can you take a look at it?
goals.why: The numbers show where buyers drop; the page audit explains why; the description is rewritten from product facts to fix what the audit found.

goals.request: keep running out of my best sellers and then sitting on boxes of stuff nobody wants. how do i get stock right
goals.why: Reorder points come from sales and lead times; restock rules are set per product group; the purchase order drafter uses the rules plan to say what to order and what to clear.

goals.request: amazon listing for my product
goals.why: Search phrases are picked from the keyword export first so the listing draft can place them in the title, bullets and backend.

goals.request: Should I even start selling on Amazon? Will I make any money after all their fees?
goals.why: Unit profit after fees answers the money question first; the viability score adds demand and competition before committing.

goals.request: my store is super slow on phones, google gives it a speed score of 28
goals.why: The speed report is read first; its findings plus the app list let the app auditor mark what to remove; the ranker orders fixes by impact.

goals.request: Lately we're getting a bunch of fake orders with stolen cards. How do I stop them?
goals.why: Fraud rules come first from the order pattern; bot access limits follow to stop card testing at the source.

goals.request: I want to A/B test my product page and find out if a new layout really sells more.
goals.why: Check there is enough traffic to test, choose the change, pick the test setup, plan one change, then read the verdict from the test results.

goals.request: move my 2,000 products from woocommerce over to shopify
goals.why: Only a generic migration planner exists: it maps fields and test imports; the product setup planner checks the Shopify side; website-content-mover plans URL redirects from the old site. No item performs the import itself.

goals.request: What should I charge per hour as a freelance designer?
goals.why: The rate is worked out from costs and billable hours first; the pricing case then explains that rate to clients and answers pushback.

goals.request: pretty sure I'm undercharging for my candles but scared raising prices will kill sales. how do I raise them without losing everyone
goals.why: Work out the floor and target price from costs, check readiness to raise, then plan a small reversible price test before rolling out.

goals.request: saas pricing tiers
goals.why: The workflow needs a business profile, so it is built first; revenue model, tiers, pricing-page layout and a price test follow in order.

goals.request: I'm about to launch an online course and have no clue what price to put on it.
goals.why: Price format and level first, then price ending and launch discount wording; the launch emails use the priced offer.

goals.request: price increase email to my clients
goals.why: Check the new price is ready to announce, then write the letter from the same offer.

goals.request: I need to send my books to the accountant for year end. What do they need and can you help me tidy it up first?
goals.why: Transactions are sorted and checked first; the reconciler then matches them and lists gaps the accountant will ask about.

goals.request: my bank statements and my spreadsheet never match, off by like $400 and I can't find where
goals.why: Match bank lines to the ledger, trace the unmatched $400, then produce clean statements once corrections are confirmed.

goals.request: cash flow forecast
goals.why: The forecast comes from the cash and sales sheet; levers to improve cash are ranked from the same data once the gap is visible.

goals.request: How much should I put aside for taxes each month now that I'm self-employed?
goals.why: A single step: the planner turns the tax share into a per-payment rule. It needs the rate from an accountant; the catalogue does not calculate tax law.

goals.request: clients keep paying late. I have 6 overdue invoices, a couple 60+ days. need the money without burning bridges
goals.why: A polite reminder goes first; payment options are reviewed for clients who can't pay in full; a firmer second note follows. The cash-chaser agent fits if they want a weekly routine.

goals.request: monthly P&L for my online shop
goals.why: Unit costs are built from invoices, sorted into cost of goods, then the P&L is built and split by new vs returning buyers before daily margin tracking.

goals.request: Help me make a budget. I want to pay off my credit card this year.
goals.why: The budget shows what can go to debt each month; the payoff plan uses that amount.

goals.request: which stocks should I buy with my $10k savings
goals.why: No item gives personal stock picks, and tools should not; the closest honest help is a check of whether an idea is investing or speculation. Expect tools to decline the pick.

goals.request: We're a 5-person startup. How many months of cash do we have left, and what happens if sales slow down?
goals.why: Runway comes from the cash sheet; the bad-case test answers the slowdown question; the cash lever ranker lists what to change first.

goals.request: Can you research the market for mobile dog grooming in my city and tell me if it's worth starting?
goals.why: Estimate the market bottom-up, pull public facts, separate proven from guessed, then write the report the go/no-go rests on.

goals.request: competitor analysis
goals.why: Both first-step options return a competitor set; the word map and white-space map read that set; the message finder turns the gaps into angles.

goals.request: I keep reading conflicting stuff about whether intermittent fasting is good for women over 40. can you dig into the actual studies and tell me what holds up
goals.why: Scope the question, find studies, write a cited report, then check each claim against its source. Research summary only, not medical advice.

goals.request: What are people actually complaining about in reviews of products like mine?
goals.why: Collect reviews of similar products first (both collectors return review quotes); the insight finder ranks the complaints; the objection sheet turns them into answers.

goals.request: questions to ask potential customers before I build anything
goals.why: Questions come from the idea brief; nothing has been interviewed yet, so there are no transcripts. After the interviews, the analyst or notes sorter turns answers into themes. idea-worth-building runs customer-interview-questions inside a before-you-build validation.

goals.request: alert me every time someone mentions my brand anywhere online, in real time
goals.why: The catalogue can scan for mentions on request, but nothing runs continuously or sends real-time alerts.

goals.request: about us page for my small business
goals.why: The true-story outline gives a first draft; its shape is checked, then it is cut and edited into plain language for the page.

goals.request: Can you make this paragraph sound less robotic? I wrote it with ChatGPT.
goals.why: The AI-style check names the tells; the plain-English pass rewrites the paragraph with those notes.

goals.request: giving a toast at my brother's wedding in 2 weeks and i'm terrible at speeches, help
goals.why: One true story becomes the toast draft; the jokes are sharpened; then it is shaped to be spoken with pauses marked.

goals.request: I want to write a book about my 20 years as a nurse but I don't know where to start.
goals.why: A project plan comes first; stories and notes are gathered into source text; the co-author turns that material into the first chapter.

goals.request: press release for our launch
goals.why: The PR planner sets key messages and a release outline, or the content drafter writes the press release itself (it has a press-release format); outreach to journalists is planned after.

goals.request: Turn these meeting notes into a clear summary I can send to the team.
goals.why: Rough notes become clean minutes first; the action register pulls owners and dates from the cleaned notes.

goals.request: blog post announcing our new feature
goals.why: The feature notes become a post brief; the post is drafted from it; a plain-English edit finishes it.

goals.request: translate my 300 page novel into Japanese
goals.why: General translators exist (article-translator chunks long texts) but a 300-page literary translation still needs a human translator and review. Partial fit.

goals.request: logo for my coffee shop
goals.why: A logo brief first; the mark plan is built from it; the strength test reviews the resulting direction. Claude plans the logo; drawing it needs an image tool.

goals.request: I have photos of my jewelry taken on my kitchen table. Can you make them look professional for my shop?
goals.why: Retouch or swap backgrounds from the home photos, then check the new set against marketplace rules and for AI artifacts. Image edits need a connected image service.

goals.request: need a little explainer video for our app for the homepage, maybe 60 sec, no budget for an agency
goals.why: The script writer needs a brand file, so the site is read first; the script plus product facts drive the build plan and clip prompts. Items are written for ads, so it is a fair but not perfect fit for a homepage explainer. product-demo-video-maker is the closest single item: a 30-60s product demo/explainer with scene plan and narration.

goals.request: infographic from my blog post
goals.why: The infographic is made from the post text; the image is then compressed for the web.

goals.request: Make me a set of matching images for my Instagram posts this month.
goals.why: Matching means shared visual rules first; prompts are written within those rules; an image tool renders them from the prompts.

goals.request: the colors on my website look kind of off and the text is hard to read. can someone check?
goals.why: The site is reviewed for readability first; a calmer palette is planned; the contrast checker tests that palette before it goes live.

goals.request: clean up the background noise in my podcast episode and cut out the long pauses
goals.why: Noise is removed from the audio; the clean audio is transcribed; the transcript drives the cut list for pauses and retakes. Noise removal needs an ElevenLabs account.

goals.request: Can you design a flyer for our bake sale on Saturday?
goals.why: Layout and type plan from the event facts, then the poster is made, then its contrast is checked.

goals.request: stabilize my shaky drone footage and color grade it in premiere for me
goals.why: No item stabilizes or color grades video or drives Premiere; edit planners only plan cuts. Tools should say so rather than offer an edit planner.

goals.request: I have an idea for an app that helps roommates split rent. How do I know if anyone actually wants it before I build it?
goals.why: Pick who to talk to, ask them, prepare questions, sort the notes, plan a commitment ask, then review the evidence for a go/change/stop call.

goals.request: product roadmap
goals.why: Customer problems become an opportunity tree; it is turned into outcomes, then a quarter plan; the update explains the choices.

goals.request: users sign up for our saas and then never come back after day 1. what do we fix first
goals.why: Find the biggest drop-off from the numbers, test the leak with a small usability test, then review metrics after the change.

goals.request: Write a PRD for a feature that lets customers schedule their deliveries.
goals.why: The PRD defines the feature; user stories with acceptance criteria are broken out from the same brief for the team.

goals.request: prioritize all these feature requests
goals.why: Requests are grouped into themes first (giving a brief); the scorer ranks them; the update explains what made the cut.

goals.request: people don't seem to love our product
goals.why: Score fit first to find the weak lever; the must-have survey then measures how disappointed users would be.

goals.request: I need a simple website for my photography business with a gallery and a contact form.
goals.why: Pages and menu are planned from the brief; the site is built with that plan; the built code is then published.

goals.request: my wordpress site got hacked, there are weird spam links everywhere, what do i do
goals.why: No item handles malware cleanup or a hacked-site recovery; the closest is reviewing theme/plugin code for security issues and turning the findings into a backup-first fix plan. A human or host security service is still needed.

goals.request: fix this python error
goals.why: A single step: the debugger reads the code and the error and returns a fix. The bug-proof workflow needs a written bug brief and is heavier than asked.

goals.request: Can you review my pull request before I merge it?
goals.why: Risks are ranked from the change, comments are fixed in the codebase, then a named person signs off on the fixed change.

goals.request: our app is getting really slow as more users join, pages take 5+ seconds to load. where do i even start
goals.why: Measure first to find the slow path; the fix uses that finding; the pull request reports before-and-after timings.

goals.request: deploy my next.js app
goals.why: Publish from the codebase, then verify the live build matches. The release workflow adds versioning and a readiness gate first.

goals.request: I want to add Stripe payments to my web app.
goals.why: The Stripe code is drafted from the billing rules; payment code then gets a security review before going live.

goals.request: build me a full uber-style ride app for iphone and android by next week
goals.why: Nothing builds a two-sided mobile marketplace in a week; the honest help is scoping the project and cutting it to a small first launch.

goals.request: I exported my sales data to a spreadsheet. Can you tell me what's interesting in it?
goals.why: Profile the file first, analyse it with the profile in hand, check the analysis document, then rank the insights.

goals.request: dashboard for my weekly numbers
goals.why: Define and build the weekly report, add trend and forecast, then put both on one dashboard.

goals.request: this spreadsheet is a disaster. duplicate rows, dates in 3 different formats, names spelled differently. need it clean before I can do anything
goals.why: Find the problems first, clean the sheet, then check the cleaned file before using it.

goals.request: Write me a SQL query that shows our top 10 customers by revenue last quarter.
goals.why: A single step: the question becomes a query. Running it needs the person's database.

goals.request: chart from my excel data
goals.why: The chart is made from the sheet; the data story explains what it shows.

goals.request: google analytics says one number, shopify says another, facebook says a third. which one is right??
goals.why: Lay the three reports side by side and explain each gap; then check the tracking setup that causes it; finally compare reported returns with real store totals.

goals.request: job description for a part-time barista
goals.why: The role is written up first; interview questions follow from the same role description.

goals.request: first time hiring. I have 40 applications for an assistant role and no idea how to pick, help
goals.why: The resumes are scored against the job to make a shortlist; an interview guide is prepared; interview notes are compared fairly to choose.

goals.request: I need to give someone on my team feedback about always being late, without making it awkward.
goals.why: Notes on the behaviour and fix come first; the feedback message uses them; it is rewritten as a request rather than an order; a plan to recognise progress follows.

goals.request: Write interview questions for a junior developer role.
goals.why: A profile of the ideal hire guides the questions; a small work test checks what questions can't.

goals.request: one of my 3 employees is underperforming and I think I need to let them go. how do I do it legally and decently
goals.why: Draft the exit plan, flag legal risks against it, plan the handover, then tell the team. Risk flags are not legal advice; local rules need checking.

goals.request: employee onboarding checklist
goals.why: new-hire-plan-builder is literally the onboarding checklist (pre-start tasks, week 1, 30/60/90); the other planners give the first-week or 90-day plan. hiring-packet-builder (job post, interview guide, offer letter) is hiring work that comes before onboarding, not part of the checklist.

goals.request: run payroll for my 4 employees this month
goals.why: No item runs payroll or files payroll taxes; only a set-up plan and questions for an accountant exist. Tools should not imply payroll gets run.

goals.request: I need to get my product made by a factory overseas but I've never done it. Where do I start?
goals.why: The tech pack is the shared spec every later step reads; factories are vetted, costs landed, samples approved, then the shipment inspection brief is written.

goals.request: compare supplier quotes
goals.why: Put the quotes on the same basis first, then score supplier risk before choosing.

goals.request: busy season's coming (black friday) and last year we were drowning in orders and support emails. how do we prep
goals.why: Forecast peak orders, size support from that forecast, line up warehouse terms and inbound stock, then audit the warehouse bill after the season.

goals.request: Plan the fastest delivery route for my 12 stops tomorrow.
goals.why: A single step from the list of stops.

goals.request: write an SOP for opening the cafe each morning
goals.why: The SOP is the whole ask; staff training on it is a natural next step, not part of the request.

goals.request: track my shipping container live on a map and text me when it lands
goals.why: Only a shared tracker sheet and warehouse notice exist; no live map or text alerts.

goals.request: Can you check this freelance contract before I sign it?
goals.why: Clause risks first, then who owns the work, then a plain summary to take to a lawyer. Not legal advice.

goals.request: privacy policy for my website
goals.why: The draft comes from business facts; a launch review flags gaps for a lawyer.

goals.request: a former client is threatening to sue me over a late delivery, what do I do
goals.why: The catalogue can read the threat, build a dated timeline and draft a reply flagged for counsel, but this needs a lawyer; tools should say so.

goals.request: Can you check whether the health claims on my supplement ads are going to get me in trouble?
goals.why: Claims are flagged first; each kept claim is then matched to its proof.

goals.request: is it ok to use pictures I found on google in my ads?
goals.why: Only a first-look screen with questions for a lawyer exists; no rights clearance or licensed-image sourcing.

goals.request: Draft an NDA for a contractor I'm bringing on.
goals.why: Draft from the deal facts, then run a quick check on the draft.

goals.request: someone left a nasty comment on our facebook page about a bad order and people are piling on. how do i respond
goals.why: Draft the public reply first; check it for tone and promises the business can't keep before posting.

goals.request: reply to bad google reviews
goals.why: Draft replies, check them for overpromising, then plan how to ask happy customers for reviews.

goals.request: We get the same 20 questions by email over and over. Can we turn them into a help center?
goals.why: Find and group the repeat questions, write help pages, check reading level, simplify, then check against real product steps.

goals.request: Customer wants a refund way outside our 30-day window. How do I say no nicely?
goals.why: Draft the reply from the case facts, then soften its tone.

goals.request: support inbox has 300 unread emails and it's just me answering them. drowning
goals.why: Sort and prioritise the backlog, draft replies, check the hard ones, then turn repeat fixes into help pages so the queue shrinks.

goals.request: put a chatbot on my website that answers customer questions 24/7
goals.why: The catalogue designs the conversation flows and builds support scripts, but nothing hosts or installs a live website chatbot.

goals.request: I have way too much on my plate this week. Help me figure out what to do first.
goals.why: See where the hours really go, pick priorities that fit those hours, then turn the plan into a first-day brief.

goals.request: inbox zero
goals.why: Set sorting rules first, clear the backlog with them, then fix names, dates and promises in the reply drafts.

goals.request: i keep procrastinating on my side project. every evening i say i'll work on it and just end up scrolling
goals.why: A tiny-habit plan with a cue tackles the evening slip; a protected focus block is planned around it.

goals.request: plan my 10 day trip to japan in april
goals.why: personal-trip-guide-builder builds a sourced day-by-day itinerary from dates, group, budget and needs. It does not book anything.

goals.request: book me a dentist appointment next week and put it in my calendar
goals.why: Booking and calendar actions are outside the catalogue; no item books appointments.

goals.request: I have a statistics exam in 3 weeks and I'm way behind. Make me a study plan.
goals.why: Map the syllabus into a learning roadmap, choose practice methods, then fit sessions with recall checks into the 3 weeks.

goals.request: flashcards from my lecture notes
goals.why: Cards are made from the notes; spaced review is a natural next step, not part of the ask.

goals.request: been on duolingo for a year learning spanish and i still can't hold a real conversation
goals.why: Only a Spanish writing tutor exists; nothing practises speaking or conversation, which is what was asked.

goals.request: Explain how compound interest works like I'm 12.
goals.why: A single tutoring step; a plain chat answer would also do. Investing-advice items do not fit.

goals.request: create an online course about watercolor painting that I can sell
goals.why: Only a mini-course web page builder and classroom lesson planners exist; there is no full paid-course design and production chain. Pricing and launch emails are available after.

goals.request: need to write a grant application for our community garden, due friday, never done one before
goals.why: Check the funder's priorities first so the proposal answers them; draft the proposal; tighten it in plain English. If the funder is already chosen, start at step 2.

goals.request: We want to thank our donors after year end and get them to give again next year.
goals.why: Thank-yous and a renewal plan come first; the next annual appeal builds on them.

goals.request: recruit volunteers for our food bank
goals.why: The volunteer program planner covers roles, recruitment channels and the sign-up funnel. Induction steps and training (the induction workflow) come after people sign up.

goals.request: Write a business plan for my food truck so I can show it to the bank.
goals.why: The plan sets the story and assumptions; a bank also wants numbers, so the financial model follows from the same brief.

goals.request: thinking about quitting my job to go full-time on my etsy shop. making about $2k a month from it right now. is that crazy?
goals.why: Size the worst case first; that plan feeds the job-exit plan; then check the plan leaves room for error.

goals.request: SWOT analysis for my business
goals.why: A single step from the business description.

goals.request: Should we switch from selling to consumers to selling to businesses? Consumer sales have been flat for a year.
goals.why: Read real progress by customer group, decide change or continue from that read, then interview business buyers before switching.

goals.request: where should my business go next
goals.why: Vague ask: find which lever (new buyers, order size, repeat) matters from the numbers, rank ideas, then set dated milestones.

goals.request: find me an investor who will put $200k into my bakery this month
goals.why: No item finds or contacts investors; the catalogue can only shape and test the pitch.
